findings.reason: §16 must either name `_authored_section_headings`/`_inside_structured_region` in its convergence on the one membership owner (`reckon/_plan_html.py`) or state why DOM element resolution is a different question, as it did for `_section_key` and `normalize_section`.
findings.text: `_authored_section_headings`, backed by `_inside_structured_region` (`reckon/mcp_views.py:2075`) with its own parent-walk machinery test, is a second owner beside `reckon/_plan_html.py:plan_headings` (the `machinery` flag from the parser) of the same authored-section membership question that `section_prose` is specified to derive from one record pass; §16 converges the prose extraction but leaves this membership test in a different module and does not name it, so a plan whose membership rule changes drifts between the two readers

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `section_prose` on `reckon/_plan_html.py` hides span arithmetic, marked-element subtraction and tag stripping behind one reader that the digests, the search text, the section response and the dispatch brief all consume.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 does not name `mcp_views._authored_section_headings`/`_inside_structured_region`, which keep a second owner of "this h2 is an authored section not inside reckon machinery" beside the parser-derived membership `section_prose` will compute.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 nets to the supplied 1481 (one public reader `section_prose` added, the interim public `strip_tags` made private) and names what it retires and why no public name can be; §20 adds no definition and says so.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §16 names the existing machinery it extends and repoints (`section_record_id`, `structured_section_spans`, `plan_headings`, `roadmap.implementable_sections`, `list_plan_reviews`, `evidence._section_key`, `ledger.normalize_section`, `doccheck._NUMBERED_SECTION_ID`, `_TAG_RE`, `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS`), and §17–§19 searched and converged the section readers and spelling grammars before §16 consumes them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16 deletes the interim slicer rather than leaving a delegator, states why no public name is retired, and adds no forwarder over existing machinery; the legacy digest forms it re-spells are a distinct grammar, not a wrapper.
